Goal
* A number's written representation alone doesn't always establish how many significant figures it has. For example, 1230 rounded to 2 significant figures is 1200, whereas 1204 rounded to 3 significant figures is also 1200.

To avoid implying that the actual measurement precision can be inferred from the input, consider replacing:

[[sig figs]] can be determined by four rules:

with:

For the purpose of this clash, [[sig figs]] is determined using the following four rules:

* Rule 1: Please change "numbers" to "digits", as these terms have distinct meanings.

* Rule 4: Please change "decimal" to "decimal point".

* Please clarify how to handle an input that contains no non-zero digits.

Output
* Please add "in [[n]]" after "figures".

* (Optional) "determined by the rules above" could be omitted to avoid repetition.

Constraints
* Please add:
1 ≤ length of [[n]] ≤ 20
[[n]] consists only of decimal digits ({{0}}–{{9}}) and at most one decimal point ({{.}}).
If present, the decimal point is neither the first nor the last character of [[n]].

Stub generator
* Please rename the variable "a" to "n" for consistency.

* Please change 5000 to 20.

Cases
* The current cases don't cover the following scenarios. Please add at least one case pair for each, using randomly generated digits rather than relying on consecutive sequences of digits:

  • [[n]] consists entirely of zeros (two or more), with no decimal point.

  • [[n]] consists entirely of zeros (two or more) and a decimal point.

  • [[n]] represents a positive integer containing leading, intermediate and trailing zeros, with at least 5 distinct groups of single/consecutive zeros (e.g. 00820992409500809000).

  • [[n]] represents a positive decimal number containing leading, intermediate and trailing zeros in the integer part, with at least one zero in the fractional part and a non-zero final digit.

Thanks.
